cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to the whole nation before they cross into the land. Now he gets down to business. These are the statutes and ordinances to follow all the days they live in the land the LORD has given them.

cards.question: First thing on Moses' list: the places where the nations in the land have served their gods. What does Moses tell Israel to do with those places?

cards.text: And these spots are EVERYWHERE: on the high mountains, on the hills, under every green tree. I spent years counting dust in a junk drawer, friend, and even I'd lose count of every green tree.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to tear down the nations' altars.
Moses says Israel may worship the LORD their God in the same way the nations served their gods.

cards.text: So if not on every hill, then where? Moses says Israel must seek a place from among all their tribes, and go there.

cards.question: The place Israel must go to worship will be chosen by the ___
What will the LORD establish that chosen place as?

cards.text: That place is where it all comes: burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, heave offerings, vow offerings, freewill offerings, and the firstborn of the herds and flocks. Friend, that's not a delivery, that's MOVING DAY.
And this is no gloomy trip. There, in the presence of the LORD their God, they and their households will eat and rejoice in all they do.

cards.question: Moses gives a reason for all that rejoicing at the chosen place. What is it?

answers.text: Their harvest was the biggest yet

cards.text: Then Moses gets real about how things work right now, out here before the Jordan. And he doesn't leave himself out either: "…as we are doing here today…"

cards.question: How does Moses describe the way things are being done right now, before the Jordan?

answers.text: Everyone does what seems right to him
Everyone waits for a word from Moses
Everyone follows the ways of Egypt

cards.question: Right now, everyone in Israel does what seems right in his own eyes. What reason does Moses give for things being this way for now?

answers.text: They haven't reached their resting place yet
They haven't built their first altar yet
The tribes haven't been counted yet

cards.text: But rest is on the way: when they cross the Jordan, the LORD will give them rest from all their enemies. Good, because doing what seems right in my own eyes was my first week in this bakery with no recipe, and the smoke alarm went off EVERY night.
Then the LORD will choose a dwelling for His Name, and everything Moses commands is to be brought there.

cards.question: Along with their sons and daughters and their menservants and maidservants, who else does Moses say will rejoice before the LORD at the chosen place?
Moses says the Levite is included because he has no portion or inheritance among them.

cards.text: Then Moses circles back to burnt offerings and says, "Be careful…" That's me checking the oven's off three times before bed.

cards.question: Moses says a burnt offering can be offered in any place a person happens to see.

cards.text: Now Moses switches from offerings to everyday meat. No altar, no vow, just a household the LORD has blessed that wants some meat.

cards.question: For that everyday meat, where does Moses say Israel may slaughter and eat it?
Moses says only the ceremonially clean may eat that everyday meat.

cards.text: They may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer, Moses says. That's a Tuesday cookie off the cooling rack, friend: no candles, no party, no reason NEEDED.

cards.question: Moses adds one firm limit on that everyday meat. They must not eat the ___
Moses brings up the tithe of grain, new wine and oil, the firstborn of the herds and flocks, and their vowed offerings. They may eat those at home within their gates, the same as everyday meat.
So where must Israel eat their tithes, firstborn and vowed offerings?

answers.text: In the LORD's presence at His chosen place
In the home of the nearest Levite
At the edge of their own fields

cards.question: The household comes to eat, and the Levite is invited again. Then Moses says to be careful not to ___ the Levites as long as Israel lives in the land.

cards.text: Moses looks ahead to when the LORD expands their territory, and someone will crave meat and say, "I want to eat meat," plain as that. Friend, I respect a man who knows EXACTLY what he wants.

cards.question: Suppose someone wants meat from their herd or flock, but the place the LORD chooses is too far from their home. Moses says they must wait until they can make the trip.

cards.text: Moses repeats himself: clean or unclean, eat it like a gazelle or deer. Then the blood rule comes back, and this time Moses says why.

cards.question: Why does Moses say Israel must not eat the blood?

answers.text: The blood belongs to the priests
The blood makes the meat unclean

cards.question: Moses says to pour the blood on the ground like water and not eat it. Do that, he says, and they'll be doing what is right in the eyes of the ___

cards.text: But holy things and vow offerings still go to the place the LORD will choose. That place is sticking with me, friend, and I could stamp it on a cookie by now.

cards.question: Burnt offerings go on the LORD's altar, meat and blood. For their other sacrifices, the blood is poured out beside the altar. What happens to the meat?

answers.text: It is burned on the altar

cards.text: Moses says be careful to obey all of it, so it may always go well with them and their children after them. Then he looks ahead to the day the LORD cuts off the nations and Israel lives in their land.

cards.question: Once those nations are destroyed, what trap does Moses warn Israel about?

answers.text: Asking how they served their gods
Asking how they farmed their land
Copying how they built their cities

cards.text: Moses says Israel must not worship the LORD their God that way, because those nations practice every abomination the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.

cards.question: Moses wraps up by telling Israel to do everything he commands. What else does he tell them about those commands?

answers.text: Not to add to them or subtract from them
To change them when the times change
To keep the parts that fit them best

cards.text: No adding, no subtracting: the one rule every recipe has, and I learned it the SMOKY way. Stay close, friend, because Moses is nowhere near done with this sermon.
